name: PineconeSearch
title: Pinecone Search
description: Search a Pinecone index by meaning, using text rather than a vector
whenToUse: Find the stored passages closest in meaning to a piece of text, in a Pinecone index that embeds its own content. Retrieval for grounding an answer, matching a question to documented material, or finding near-duplicates. The index must have been created with an embedding model attached; one holding vectors computed elsewhere cannot be searched this way, and searching the platform's own knowledge base is a different step entirely.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Trigger signal from the upstream node

outputs.name: matches
outputs.description: Matching records, best first, each with id, score and the requested fields

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: How many matches came back, after any score threshold

indexName.title: Index Name
indexName.description: The Pinecone index to search. It must have been created with an embedding model attached, since the query text is embedded by Pinecone rather than beforehand.

query.title: Query Text
query.description: The text to search for. Pinecone embeds it and returns the closest stored records.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Search inside one namespace. Leave blank to search the index's default namespace.

fields.title: Fields To Return
fields.description: Which stored fields come back with each match, comma-separated. Must include the text field the index embeds (chunk_text unless the index says otherwise), or matches arrive as scores attached to nothing.

topK.title: Top K Results
topK.description: How many matches to ask Pinecone for, before any score threshold

scoreThreshold.title: Score Threshold
scoreThreshold.description: Drop matches scoring below this. 0 keeps everything Pinecone returned. Applied here rather than by Pinecone, which has no minimum-score parameter.

metadataFilter.title: Metadata Filter
metadataFilter.description: A JSON object restricting matches by stored field, e.g. {"category": "support"}. A malformed filter is ignored rather than failing the search.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: pinecone
package.packageFile:
name: pinecone
displayName: Pinecone
version: 2.0.0
description: Vector search over Pinecone, with embedding done by Pinecone

# WHY THIS PACKAGE COULD FINALLY BECOME A MANIFEST, and why the reason was not the one
# recorded in the backlog for months.
#
# The blocker was never "Pinecone has no REST API" — it always had one. It was that the old
# nodes CONSUMED an embedding service over a service edge: query and upload both took a
# vector from a neighbouring embedding node, and no manifest call can make that hop. Adding
# REST would not have helped, because the missing piece was upstream of the request.
#
# Pinecone's INTEGRATED INFERENCE removes the hop entirely. An index created with an
# embedding model attached accepts TEXT and embeds it server-side, so `/records/*` takes the
# raw string and there is no vector to source from anywhere. The service edge disappears
# rather than being expressed.
#
# THE COST, and it is a real one: integrated inference only works on an index created WITH a
# model and a field_map. An index holding externally-computed vectors cannot use these
# endpoints. Repointing an existing workflow means recreating the index, which is why the
# node types changed rather than being reused (see each node.yaml).

category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749139513/gravity/icons/pinecone.png

allowedHosts:
  # The control plane, where an index is looked up by name.
  - api.pinecone.io
  # The DATA plane host is per-index and only learned at run time — a name like
  # `kb-a1b2c3.svc.aped-4627-b74a.pinecone.io`. Two labels deep, so `*.pinecone.io` (one
  # level only) would refuse it: `**` is required and is the weaker rule on purpose. Still
  # bounded to Pinecone's own domain, which is what allowedHosts is for.
  - "**.pinecone.io"

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.7.0"
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  transport: [json]
  # Pinecone's record upsert takes newline-delimited JSON: one document per line, no array.
  encoding: [ndjson]

credentials.pineconeCredential.yaml:
# One key. The retired credential also carried an `environment` field ("us-east-1-aws"),
# which the old SDK needed to build a host. The REST path looks the index up by name on the
# control plane and is TOLD its host, so asking for the environment as well would be asking
# for something already known, and getting it wrong produced a confusing DNS failure rather
# than a useful message.

name: pineconeCredential
displayName: Pinecone
description: >-
  Pinecone API key, from the console under API Keys. The key's project must contain the
  index the node names.

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Pinecone API key
    placeholder: "pcsk_..."

shared.index.yaml:
# THE HOST LOOKUP, shared because every node in this package needs it and none can skip it.
#
# Pinecone's data plane lives on a host that is unique per index and not derivable from the
# index name: `kb-a1b2c3.svc.aped-4627-b74a.pinecone.io`. The old SDK hid this behind
# `pinecone.index(name)`, which is why the retired nodes only ever asked for a NAME.
#
# Keeping that config field is worth one extra request. The alternative is making an author
# paste a host they have to go and find, and which changes if the index is recreated.

describe:
  name: describeIndex
  method: GET
  url: "https://api.pinecone.io/indexes/{{ config.indexName }}"
  transport: json
  credential: { $ref: index#credential }
  headers:
    X-Pinecone-Api-Version: "2025-04"
  error:
    # A 404 here means the index does not exist IN THIS KEY'S PROJECT, which is the single
    # most common setup mistake: the right name in the wrong project. Said plainly, because
    # the raw reply is a generic not-found that sends people looking at the wrong thing.
    when: "return !response.host"
    message: >-
      return 'Pinecone index "' + config.indexName + '" was not found, or the API key belongs
      to a different project. Check the index name and that this key is from the same project.'

# apiKeyHeader rather than bearer: Pinecone reads `Api-Key`, and a bearer token is silently
# ignored rather than rejected, so the failure looks like a permissions problem.
credential:
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: Api-Key
  value: "{{ credentials.pineconeCredential.apiKey }}"

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml's order.
#
# `result.hits` is the integrated-inference shape and it is NOT the shape the old `/query`
# endpoint returned: that one gave `matches` with `id`/`score`/`metadata`, this one gives
# `hits` with `_id`/`_score`/`fields`. Flattened here so a downstream template reads
# `match.id` and `match.text` rather than leading-underscore vendor spelling.

- emit: matches
  value: >-
    return (response.result.hits || [])
      .filter(h => Number(h._score) >= (Number(config.scoreThreshold) || 0))
      .map(h => Object.assign(
        { id: h._id, score: Math.round(Number(h._score) * 1000) / 1000 },
        h.fields || {}
      ))

# Counted AFTER the threshold, because a caller branching on "did we find anything" means
# anything that survived filtering. Recomputed rather than read off the first row, since an
# events row cannot see what a sibling emitted.
- emit: count
  value: >-
    return (response.result.hits || [])
      .filter(h => Number(h._score) >= (Number(config.scoreThreshold) || 0)).length
files.config.yaml:
# Transcribed from the retired node, minus two fields that integrated inference makes
# meaningless:
#
#   includeValues   returned the raw embedding alongside each match. There is no client-side
#                   vector in this design, and shipping thousands of floats into a workflow
#                   was context bloat nothing downstream could use.
#   includeMetadata  became `fields`, below. Pinecone now returns exactly the stored fields
#                   you name rather than a whole metadata blob, so the question changed from
#                   "include it?" to "which ones?".

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [indexName, query]
  properties:
    indexName:
      type: string
      title: Index Name
      description: >-
        The Pinecone index to search. It must have been created with an embedding model
        attached, since the query text is embedded by Pinecone rather than beforehand.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    query:
      type: string
      title: Query Text
      description: The text to search for. Pinecone embeds it and returns the closest stored records.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    namespace:
      type: string
      title: Namespace
      description: Search inside one namespace. Leave blank to search the index's default namespace.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    fields:
      type: string
      title: Fields To Return
      description: >-
        Which stored fields come back with each match, comma-separated. Must include the
        text field the index embeds (chunk_text unless the index says otherwise), or matches
        arrive as scores attached to nothing.
      default: chunk_text
      ui:field: template

    topK:
      type: number
      title: Top K Results
      description: How many matches to ask Pinecone for, before any score threshold
      default: 10
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100

    scoreThreshold:
      type: number
      title: Score Threshold
      description: >-
        Drop matches scoring below this. 0 keeps everything Pinecone returned. Applied here
        rather than by Pinecone, which has no minimum-score parameter.
      default: 0.3
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 1
      step: 0.05

    metadataFilter:
      type: string
      title: Metadata Filter
      description: >-
        A JSON object restricting matches by stored field, e.g. {"category": "support"}. A
        malformed filter is ignored rather than failing the search.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
"ui:order":
  [indexName, namespace, query, fields, topK, scoreThreshold, metadataFilter]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    required: true
    description: Trigger signal from the upstream node

outputs:
  # The old node emitted a single `output` array. Split in two here because a downstream
  # step almost always wants one or the other: the matches to loop over, or the count to
  # branch on. Reaching for `.length` in a template worked, but "did the search find
  # anything" is a question worth having an answer to.
  - name: matches
    type: array
    description: Matching records, best first, each with id, score and the requested fields

  - name: count
    type: number
    description: How many matches came back, after any score threshold

credentials:
  - name: pineconeCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Pinecone
files.node.yaml:
# Transcribed from _legacy/nodes/pinecone/src/PineconeQuery, with the embedding step removed
# rather than reimplemented: Pinecone now embeds the query text itself.

type: PineconeSearch

# NOT the old `PineconeQuery`. The old node embedded with whatever model its embedding edge
# provided; this one embeds with the model bound to the INDEX. Same text in, different
# vector, so the same query can rank differently. A saved workflow stores the type string,
# and silently changing which model interprets a search is not a change to make invisibly.

kind: PromiseNode

name: Pinecone Search
category: Knowledge & Vectors
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749139513/gravity/icons/pinecone.png
color: "#4B5563"

description: Search a Pinecone index by meaning, using text rather than a vector

whenToUse: >-
  Find the stored passages closest in meaning to a piece of text, in a Pinecone index that
  embeds its own content. Retrieval for grounding an answer, matching a question to
  documented material, or finding near-duplicates. The index must have been created with an
  embedding model attached; one holding vectors computed elsewhere cannot be searched this
  way, and searching the platform's own knowledge base is a different step entirely.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A READ, and deterministic for a given index state, so reuse is safe within a run and
  # skips nothing. The index changing between runs is what cache lifetime is for, not a
  # reason to refuse caching.
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
# Needs a REAL index created with an embedding model attached. An index holding
# externally-computed vectors returns a 400 from /records/search, and that is the single
# most useful thing this fixture can catch: it is the one setup difference between this node
# and the one it replaces.
#
# Asserts SHAPE, never particular records: the index's contents are the tester's, so
# asserting a title would only prove whose account ran it.

testData:
  config:
    indexName: "{{ env.PINECONE_INDEX }}"
    query: What is the return policy for damaged items?
    fields: chunk_text
    topK: 5
    scoreThreshold: 0
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    # The two-call chain worked: a host was discovered and searched. An empty array is a
    # legitimate answer here, so the assertion is about the TYPE, not the length.
    matches: "return Array.isArray(output.matches)"
    count: "return typeof output.count === 'number' && output.count === output.matches.length"
